title: The future of English
paragraphs: You're learning English, aren't you? You might think you can work out the grammar and have built up a vast vocabulary, but then you come across an expression like 'plos'. According to the online Urban Dictionary, it means 'parents looking over shoulder'. You can blame teenagers for that. They have a code of their own, including 'text speak' when they're online or using their phones.

Text speak has a lot to do with inventing cool new terms - and these change quickly. Maybe you shouldn't be surprised if an English friend says you sound a bit old-fashioned. The modal verb 'shall' is on the way out because 'will' sounds more natural these days. Bas Aarts, Professor of English linguistics at University College London says, "If you have two words which more or less express the same meaning, one of the two words will get pushed out of the language."

People have been shying away from using the modal 'must' because it sounds authoritarian and people are choosing to express obligation in different ways. It sounds nicer to soften obligation by saying 'might'. For example, "You might like to read this article."

Progressive tenses - formed from the verb 'be' and the suffix 'ing' - are used for ongoing situations, for example, 'I'm writing this article for you to read'. But its use has been increasing rapidly. Bas Aarts says that this might have to do with advertising. A fast-food chain uses the expression 'I'm loving it' in English-speaking countries. But the verb 'love' expresses a state of being - as opposed to doing - and is usually used in the simple form, for example, 'I love it'. These days, people are using stative verbs in the progressive more and more.

Before you despair and throw your English book in the bin, be assured that some words take a very long time to change. According to Professor Mark Pagel at Reading University in the UK, pronouns like 'I', 'you' and 'we' evolve slowly - a thousand years ago we would be using similar or sometimes identical sounds. Nouns and adjectives, on the other hand, get replaced rapidly - and in 500 years or so we'll probably be using different words to the ones we have now. But let's leave that problem for the future generations.

vocabulary.entry: work out [phr.] /wɜːk aʊt/ 弄清楚；解决 (固定搭配)
vocabulary.example: I need to work out the answer to this problem.
vocabulary.translation: 我需要弄清楚这个问题的答案。

vocabulary.example: Good grammar is essential for clear writing.
vocabulary.translation: 良好的语法对于清晰的写作至关重要。

vocabulary.example: She has a vast knowledge of art history.
vocabulary.translation: 她对艺术史有广博的知识。

vocabulary.example: Reading helps expand your vocabulary.
vocabulary.translation: 阅读有助于扩大你的词汇量。

vocabulary.example: This expression is commonly used in spoken English.
vocabulary.translation: 这个表达在英语口语中很常用。

vocabulary.example: Urban areas are often more crowded than rural ones.
vocabulary.translation: 城市地区通常比农村更拥挤。

vocabulary.example: Teenagers often use slang that adults don't understand.
vocabulary.translation: 青少年经常使用成年人听不懂的俚语。

vocabulary.example: Look up the word in a dictionary if you don't know it.
vocabulary.translation: 如果你不认识这个词，就查字典。

vocabulary.example: The magazine is aimed at teenagers.
vocabulary.translation: 这本杂志面向青少年。

vocabulary.example: They communicated using a secret code.
vocabulary.translation: 他们用秘密代码进行交流。

vocabulary.example: He invented a device that cleans itself.
vocabulary.translation: 他发明了一种可以自我清洁的装置。

vocabulary.example: The medical term for high blood pressure is hypertension.
vocabulary.translation: 高血压的医学术语是hypertension。

vocabulary.entry: old-fashioned [adj.] /ˌəʊld ˈfæʃənd/ 老土的；过时的
vocabulary.example: His clothes look old-fashioned.
vocabulary.translation: 他的衣服看起来很老土。

vocabulary.entry: modal verb [n.] /ˈməʊdəl vɜːb/ 情态动词 (语法术语)
vocabulary.example: "Can", "could", "may" and "might" are modal verbs.
vocabulary.translation: can、could、may和might都是情态动词。

vocabulary.entry: on the way out [phr.] /ɒn ðə weɪ aʊt/ 逐渐过时；即将被淘汰 (口语；固定搭配)
vocabulary.example: Landline telephones are on the way out.
vocabulary.translation: 固定电话正在逐渐被淘汰。

vocabulary.example: She studied linguistics at university.
vocabulary.translation: 她在大学学习语言学。

vocabulary.entry: more or less [phr.] /mɔːr ɔː les/ 或多或少；大体上 (固定搭配)
vocabulary.example: The job is more or less finished.
vocabulary.translation: 这项工作大体上完成了。

vocabulary.entry: push out of [phr.] /pʊʃ aʊt əv/ 挤出；驱逐出 (固定搭配)
vocabulary.example: Small businesses are being pushed out of the market.
vocabulary.translation: 小企业正被挤出市场。

vocabulary.entry: shy away from [phr.] /ʃaɪ əˈweɪ frɒm/ 避免；回避 (固定搭配)
vocabulary.example: He shied away from discussing his past.
vocabulary.translation: 他回避谈论自己的过去。

vocabulary.entry: authoritarian [adj.] /ɔːˌθɒrɪˈteəriən/ 专断的；专制的 (书面语)
vocabulary.example: His authoritarian style of management made him unpopular.
vocabulary.translation: 他专制的管理风格使他不受欢迎。

vocabulary.example: You have an obligation to tell the truth.
vocabulary.translation: 你有义务说实话。

vocabulary.example: He softened his tone when speaking to the child.
vocabulary.translation: 他同孩子说话时放柔和了语气。

vocabulary.entry: progressive tenses [n. pl.] /prəˈɡresɪv tensɪz/ 进行时态 (语法术语；单数: progressive tense)
vocabulary.example: The present progressive tense describes actions happening now.
vocabulary.translation: 现在进行时描述正在发生的动作。

vocabulary.entry: stative verb [n.] /ˈsteɪtɪv vɜːb/ 静态动词 (语法术语)
vocabulary.example: "Believe" is a stative verb and is rarely used in the progressive form.
vocabulary.translation: "Believe"是一个静态动词，很少用于进行时态。

vocabulary.example: Never despair; things will get better.
vocabulary.translation: 永远不要绝望；情况会好转的。

vocabulary.entry: evolve [v.] /ɪˈvɒlv/ 进化；演变；发展 (书面语)
vocabulary.example: Language evolves constantly over time.
vocabulary.translation: 语言随着时间的推移不断演变。

vocabulary.entry: identical [adj.] /aɪˈdentɪkəl/ 相同的；完全同样的
vocabulary.example: The two pictures are nearly identical.
vocabulary.translation: 这两幅画几乎一模一样。

sentences.chinese: 这得怪青少年们。

sentences.chinese: 他们有自己的暗语，包括在上网或使用手机时用的“文本语言”。

sentences.english: Text speak has a lot to do with inventing cool new terms - and these change quickly.
sentences.chinese: 文本语言与发明很酷的新术语有很大关系——而且这些术语变化得很快。

sentences.english: Maybe you shouldn't be surprised if an English friend says you sound a bit old-fashioned.
sentences.chinese: 如果一位英国朋友说你听起来有点老土，也许你不应该感到惊讶。

sentences.english: The modal verb 'shall' is on the way out because 'will' sounds more natural these days.
sentences.chinese: 情态动词“shall”正逐渐过时，因为如今“will”听起来更自然。

sentences.english: Bas Aarts, Professor of English linguistics at University College London says, "If you have two words which more or less express the same meaning, one of the two words will get pushed out of the language."
sentences.chinese: 伦敦大学学院的英语语言学教授巴斯·阿茨说：“如果你有两个或多或少表达相同意思的词，那么这两个词中的一个将会被挤出这种语言。”

sentences.english: People have been shying away from using the modal 'must' because it sounds authoritarian and people are choosing to express obligation in different ways.
sentences.chinese: 人们一直避免使用情态动词“must”，因为它听起来很专横，而且人们正选择用不同的方式来表达责任。

sentences.english: It sounds nicer to soften obligation by saying 'might'.
sentences.chinese: 用“might”来缓和义务的语气听起来更好。

sentences.english: For example, "You might like to read this article."
sentences.chinese: 例如，“你或许会想读这篇文章。”

sentences.english: Progressive tenses - formed from the verb 'be' and the suffix 'ing' - are used for ongoing situations, for example, 'I'm writing this article for you to read'.
sentences.chinese: 进行时态——由动词“be”和后缀“ing”构成——用于表示正在进行的情况，例如，“我正在写这篇文章供你阅读。”

sentences.english: But its use has been increasing rapidly.
sentences.chinese: 但它的使用一直在迅速增加。

sentences.english: Bas Aarts says that this might have to do with advertising.
sentences.chinese: 巴斯·阿茨说，这可能与广告有关。

sentences.english: A fast-food chain uses the expression 'I'm loving it' in English-speaking countries.
sentences.chinese: 一家快餐连锁店在英语国家使用“我就喜欢”这种表达。

sentences.english: But the verb 'love' expresses a state of being - as opposed to doing - and is usually used in the simple form, for example, 'I love it'.
sentences.chinese: 但是动词“love”表达的是一种状态——而不是动作——并且通常用一般现在时形式，例如，“我喜欢”。

sentences.english: These days, people are using stative verbs in the progressive more and more.
sentences.chinese: 如今，人们越来越多地在进行时态中使用静态动词。

sentences.english: Before you despair and throw your English book in the bin, be assured that some words take a very long time to change.
sentences.chinese: 在你绝望并把你的英语书扔进垃圾桶之前，请放心，有些单词需要很长时间才会发生变化。

sentences.english: According to Professor Mark Pagel at Reading University in the UK, pronouns like 'I', 'you' and 'we' evolve slowly - a thousand years ago we would be using similar or sometimes identical sounds.
sentences.chinese: 根据英国雷丁大学的马克·佩格尔教授的说法，像“I”、“you”和“we”这样的代词变化得很慢——一千年前，我们使用的发音与之相似，有时甚至相同。

sentences.english: Nouns and adjectives, on the other hand, get replaced rapidly - and in 500 years or so we'll probably be using different words to the ones we have now.
sentences.chinese: 另一方面，名词和形容词的更新换代却很快——大约500年后，我们可能会使用与现在不同的单词。

sentences.english: But let's leave that problem for the future generations.
sentences.chinese: 但我们还是把这个问题留给后代吧。
